meta_desc: Class 5 Weight and Capacity worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 8): kg and g, L and mL, converting, comparing and problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Convert to one unit, then compare or add.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 2 kg 450 g = 2,450 g; 1.5 L = 1,500 mL.
  • Add or subtract after changing to the same unit.

Examples

Example

A bucket holds 12 L. How many 500 mL mugs fill it?

12 L = 12,000 mL

12,000 ÷ 500

Answer: 24 mugs

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using 100 g = 1 kg1,000 g make 1 kg.
Adding kg and g directlyChange both to grams first.

faq.q: How many grams are in 2.5 kg?

faq.a: How much a container can hold.

items.q: Convert. 4 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1,000: 4 × 1,000 = 4,000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 4 kg = 4,000 g.

items.q: Convert. 6,000 mL = ☐ l
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1,000: 6,000 ÷ 1,000 = 6. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 6,000 mL = 6 L.

items.q: Convert. 2.5 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1,000: 2.5 × 1,000 = 2,500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.5 kg = 2,500 g.

items.q: Convert. 1.5 L = ☐ ml
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1,000: 1.5 × 1,000 = 1,500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.5 L = 1,500 mL.

items.q: Convert. 350 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1,000: 350 ÷ 1,000 = 0.35. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 350 g = 0.35 kg. Check: 0.35 kg is a bit more than a quarter of a kilogram.

items.q: Convert. 750 mL = ☐ l
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1,000: 750 ÷ 1,000 = 0.75. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 750 mL = 0.75 L.

items.q: Convert. 0.25 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1,000: 0.25 × 1,000 = 250. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.25 kg = 250 g.

items.q: Convert. 3.2 L = ☐ ml
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1,000: 3.2 × 1,000 = 3,200. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3.2 L = 3,200 mL.

items.q: Convert. 80 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1,000: 80 ÷ 1,000 = 0.08. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 80 g = 0.08 kg. You need a 0 in the tenths place.

items.q: Convert. 1,250 mL = ☐ l
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1,000: 1,250 ÷ 1,000 = 1.25. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 1,250 mL = 1.25 L.

items.q: Convert. 2 kg 50 g = ☐ kg
Work out 1.2 L + 600 mL. Give your answer in litres.
items.e: Use one unit first: 600 mL = 0.6 L. Then 1.2 + 0.6 = 1.8 L. 601.2 L adds the numbers without converting.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg 600 g = 1,600 g, 1.5 kg = 1,500 g and 0.95 kg = 950 g. 1,600 g is the heaviest.

items.q: Which list goes from the smallest to the largest capacity?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 0.3 L = 300 mL and 0.5 L = 500 mL. 300 < 450 < 500.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of some carrots. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g and there are 4 spaces, so each mark is 50 g. The needle is 3 marks past 600 g: 600 + 150 = 750 g. 750 ÷ 1,000 = 0.75 kg. (0.63 kg counts each mark as 10 g.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of potatoes. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 5 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 5 = 0.2 kg (200 g). The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 2 + 0.6 = 2.6 kg. (2.3 kg counts each mark as 0.1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a parcel. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 4 = 0.25 kg (250 g). The needle is 3 marks past 1 kg: 1 + 0.75 = 1.75 kg. (1.3 kg counts each mark as 0.1 kg.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL and there are 5 spaces, so each line is 50 mL. The water is 2 lines above 750 mL: 750 + 100 = 850 mL. 850 ÷ 1,000 = 0.85 L. (0.77 L counts each line as 10 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mL and there are 5 spaces, so each line is 100 mL. The water is 3 lines above 1,000 mL: 1,300 mL. 1,300 ÷ 1,000 = 1.3 L. (1.15 L counts each line as 50 mL.)

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 2 litres?
items.e: Each line is 100 mL. The water is at 1,200 mL. 2 litres = 2,000 mL. 2,000 − 1,200 = 800 mL more. (1,200 mL is the water already in the jug.)
The pencil starts at 0. It ends 4 small marks past 7 cm. 7 cm = 70 mm, and 70 + 4 = 74 mm. (80 mm reads the next number, 8, instead of counting the small marks.)
The crayon starts at 2 cm, not 0. It ends at 8 cm 3 mm. 83 mm − 20 mm = 63 mm = 6 cm 3 mm. (8 cm 3 mm forgets that the crayon does not start at 0.)
The eraser starts at 1 cm (10 mm) and ends at 48 mm. 48 − 10 = 38 mm. (48 mm forgets that it starts at 1 cm. 30 mm counts only the whole centimetres.)
The ribbon ends 5 small marks past 10 cm. 10 cm = 100 mm, and 100 + 5 = 105 mm. (150 mm reads 10 cm 5 mm as 1 and 50.)
The pencil ends 7 small marks past 9 cm, so it is 9 cm 7 mm (97 mm). 9 cm and 10 cm are only to the nearest centimetre. 97 cm uses the wrong unit.
The crayon ends 8 small marks past 5 cm, so it is 5 cm 8 mm (58 mm). 6 cm is the nearest whole centimetre, but 5 cm 8 mm is more accurate.
Each kilogram is split into 10 spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 4 marks past 1 kg: 1 kg and 4 × 100 = 400 g, so 1 kg 400 g. (1 kg 40 g counts each mark as 10 g.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of potatoes. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 2 kg and 3 × 250 = 750 g, so 2 kg 750 g. (2 kg 300 g counts each mark as 100 g.)
Each kilogram is split into 5 spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 5 = 200 g. The needle is 3 marks past 3 kg: 3 kg and 3 × 200 = 600 g, so 3 kg 600 g. (3 kg 300 g counts each mark as 100 g.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bunch of bananas. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g and there are 4 spaces between them, so each mark is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 600: 600 + 50 = 650 g. (610 g counts each mark as 10 g, and 700 g counts each mark as 100 g.)

The numbers go up by 100 g and there are 5 spaces between them, so each mark is 100 ÷ 5 = 20 g. The needle is 3 marks past 300: 300 + 60 = 360 g. (330 g counts each mark as 10 g. 400 g reads the next number.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of flour. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g and there are 5 spaces between them, so each mark is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 g. The needle is 3 marks past 1,500: 1,500 + 300 = 1,800 g. (1,530 g counts each mark as 10 g.)
Each mark is 100 g, so the needle is at 1 kg 300 g = 1,300 g. 2 kg = 2,000 g. 2,000 − 1,300 = 700 g more.

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in L and mL.
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mL and there are 2 spaces between them, so each line is 500 ÷ 2 = 250 mL. The water is 1 line above 1,000: 1,000 + 250 = 1,250 mL. (1 L 100 mL counts each line as 100 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL and there are 4 spaces between them, so each line is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 mL. The water is 3 lines above 600: 600 + 150 = 750 mL. (630 mL counts each line as 10 mL, and 900 mL counts each line as 100 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in L and mL.
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 2 lines above 2 L: 2 L and 2 × 250 = 500 mL, so 2 L 500 mL. (2 L 200 mL counts each line as 100 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in millilitres.
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 3 lines above 1 L: 1 L and 3 × 250 = 750 mL, so 1 L 750 mL. (1,300 mL counts each line as 100 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mL and there are 5 spaces between them, so each line is 100 ÷ 5 = 20 mL. The water is 2 lines above 400: 400 + 40 = 440 mL. (420 mL counts each line as 10 mL.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL and there are 5 spaces between them, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 mL. The water is 2 lines above 750: 750 + 100 = 850 mL. (770 mL counts each line as 10 mL.)

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 2 L?
items.e: Each line is 100 mL, so the water is at 1,400 mL. 2 L = 2,000 mL. 2,000 − 1,400 = 600 mL more. (1,400 mL is the water already in the jug.)

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000, so 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams. A 1 kg bag of flour is as heavy as 1,000 paper clips.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1,000 millilitres make 1 litre. Four 250 mL glasses fill a 1 L jug.

items.q: Convert. 4 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1,000: 4 × 1,000 = 4,000. So 4 kg = 4,000 g. (400 g multiplies by 100, but 1 kg is 1,000 g.)

items.q: Convert. 6 L = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1,000: 6 × 1,000 = 6,000. So 6 L = 6,000 mL. (600 mL uses × 100. A litre has 1,000 millilitres.)

items.q: Convert. 9 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1,000: 9 × 1,000 = 9,000. So 9 kg = 9,000 g.

items.q: Convert. 2 L = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1,000: 2 × 1,000 = 2,000. So 2 L = 2,000 mL.

items.q: Convert. 15 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1,000: 15 × 1,000 = 15,000. So 15 kg = 15,000 g. (1,500 g multiplies by 100 instead of 1,000.)

items.q: Convert. 10 L = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1,000: 10 × 1,000 = 10,000. So 10 L = 10,000 mL. Multiplying by 1,000 puts 3 zeros after 10.

items.q: Convert. 3 kg 250 g = ☐ g
Convert. 1 L 500 mL = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. 1,000 + 500 = 1,500 mL. (600 mL uses 1 L = 100 mL, and 1,005 mL would be 1 L 5 mL.)

items.q: Convert. 2 kg 80 g = ☐ g
items.e: 2 kg = 2,000 g. 2,000 + 80 = 2,080 g. The 0 holds the hundreds place. (2,800 g would be 2 kg 800 g.)

items.q: Convert. 4 L 5 mL = ☐ mL
items.e: 4 L = 4,000 mL. 4,000 + 5 = 4,005 mL. (4,500 mL would be 4 L 500 mL, and 4,050 mL would be 4 L 50 mL.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of apples in kilograms. What is the mass in grams?
items.e: The needle points to 2 kg. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so 2 × 1,000 = 2,000 g. (200 g uses × 100.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a pumpkin. What is the mass in grams?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 2 equal spaces, so each mark is half a kilogram, 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 3 kg: 3,000 + 500 = 3,500 g. (3,050 g reads the half mark as 50 g.)

items.q: The jug is marked in litres. How much water is in it, in millilitres?
items.e: The water is at 2 L. 1 L = 1,000 mL, so 2 × 1,000 = 2,000 mL. (200 mL uses × 100.)

items.q: The jug is marked in litres. How much water is in it, in millilitres?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 equal spaces, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 2 lines above 1 L: 1,000 + 250 + 250 = 1,500 mL. (1,200 mL counts each line as 100 mL.)

items.q: Find the missing number. 7,000 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so count the thousands: 7,000 g is 7 groups of 1,000 g, which is 7 kg. (70 kg uses 1 kg = 100 g.)

items.q: Find the missing number. 8,000 mL = ☐ L
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. 8,000 mL is 8 groups of 1,000 mL, which is 8 L. (8,000 L forgets to change the unit.)

items.q: Convert. 5 L 750 mL = ☐ mL
Convert. 12 kg 400 g = ☐ g
3 L = ? cm³
7 L = ? cm³
12 L = ? cm³
250 mL = ? cm³
items.e: 1 mL = 1 cm³, so 250 mL = 250 cm³. Do not multiply or divide by 1,000.

items.q: 600 mL = ? cm³
items.e: 1 mL = 1 cm³, so 600 mL = 600 cm³. Do not multiply or divide by 1,000.

items.q: Write 2,450 cm³ in litres and millilitres.
items.e: 2,450 cm³ = 2,450 mL = 2,000 mL + 450 mL = 2 L 450 mL. The thousands are the litres.

items.q: Write 3,080 cm³ in litres and millilitres.
items.e: 3,080 cm³ = 3,080 mL = 3,000 mL + 80 mL = 3 L 80 mL. The thousands are the litres.

items.q: Write 1,605 cm³ in litres and millilitres.
items.e: 1,605 cm³ = 1,605 mL = 1,000 mL + 605 mL = 1 L 605 mL. The thousands are the litres.

items.q: 1 L 80 mL = ? cm³
4 L 250 mL = ? cm³
How many litres of water can this container hold when full?
How many litres of water can this container hold when full?
A container is 30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 25 cm high. What is its capacity in litres?
A container is 40 cm long, 25 cm wide and 20 cm high. What is its capacity in litres?
A carton is 15 cm long, 12 cm wide and 20 cm high. What is its capacity in litres and millilitres?
A carton is 18 cm long, 10 cm wide and 15 cm high. What is its capacity in litres and millilitres?
Which is equal to 1 L 50 mL?
items.e: 1 L 50 mL = 1,000 mL + 50 mL = 1,050 mL = 1,050 cm³. 1,500 cm³ would be 1 L 500 mL.

items.q: A pancake recipe for 4 people uses 300 mL of milk. Kabir makes pancakes for 8 people. How much milk does he need?
items.e: 8 people is double 4 people, so double the milk: 2 × 300 = 600 mL. (2,400 mL multiplies by 8. 150 mL halves instead of doubling.)

items.q: A recipe for Anzac biscuits uses 150 g of flour. Simran makes 3 batches. How much flour does she use?
items.e: 3 batches: 3 × 150 = 450 g. (153 g adds 3 instead of multiplying.)

items.q: A recipe needs 1.5 kg of potatoes. Ayaan has 900 g. How many more grams does he need?
items.e: 1.5 kg = 1,500 g. 1,500 − 900 = 600 g more. (150 g treats 1.5 kg as 1,050 g. 2,400 g adds instead of finding the difference.)

items.q: To make a jug of cordial, you mix 250 mL of cordial with 1.75 L of water. How much drink does that make?
items.e: Use one unit: 1.75 L = 1,750 mL. 250 + 1,750 = 2,000 mL = 2 L. (251.75 mL adds the numbers without converting.)

items.q: At the athletics carnival, Isha jumps 3 m 45 cm in the long jump. How far is that in centimetres?
In the long jump, Tara jumps 3 m 20 cm and Aarav jumps 2 m 95 cm. How much further does Tara jump?
items.e: Use centimetres: 320 − 295 = 25 cm. (1 m 75 cm takes 20 from 95 instead of regrouping 1 m as 100 cm.)

items.q: Four students do the long jump at the athletics carnival. Ishaan jumps 2.9 m, Priya jumps 285 cm, Karan jumps 3 m 5 cm and Tara jumps 3.1 m. Who jumps the furthest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 2.9 m = 290 cm, 3 m 5 cm = 305 cm and 3.1 m = 310 cm. 310 cm is the furthest, so Tara wins. 3.1 m is 3 m 10 cm, which is more than 3 m 5 cm.

items.q: In the 4 × 100 m relay, each runner runs 100 m. How far does the whole team run in kilometres?
The school cross-country course is 2.5 km long. Nisha has run 1,800 m. How far does she still have to run?
items.e: 2.5 km = 2,500 m. 2,500 − 1,800 = 700 m. (4,300 m adds instead. 1,300 m takes 5 from 8 instead of regrouping.)

items.q: Neha’s water bottle holds 750 mL. On a hot day she fills it and drinks it all 4 times. How many litres does she drink?
items.e: 4 × 750 = 3,000 mL. 1 L = 1,000 mL, so 3,000 mL = 3 L. (3,000 L forgets to change mL into L.)

items.q: Anika’s school runs the Charity Run. The route is 5 km long. How many metres is that?
Anika’s backpack has a mass of 4 kg. Her lunch has a mass of 600 g. What is the total mass in grams?
items.e: Change to one unit first: 4 kg = 4,000 g. 4,000 + 600 = 4,600 g. (604 g adds 4 + 600 without converting, and 1,000 g uses 4 kg = 400 g.)

items.q: A 2 L carton of milk is poured into glasses that hold 250 mL each. How many glasses can be filled?
items.e: 2 L = 2,000 mL. 2,000 ÷ 250 = 8 glasses. Check: 4 glasses make 1 L. (500 multiplies 2 × 250, and 125 divides 250 by 2.)

items.q: Sneha has 2 m of ribbon. She cuts it into pieces that are 20 cm long. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: 2 m = 200 cm. 200 ÷ 20 = 10 pieces. (1 piece uses 2 m = 20 cm, and 40 multiplies 2 × 20.)

items.q: A portage on a canoe trip is 1.2 km long. How many metres is the portage?
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m, so 1.2 × 1,000 = 1,200 m. (120 m multiplies by 100, and 1,002 m reads 1.2 km as 1 km 2 m.)

items.q: Four friends each bring a 750 mL water bottle on a field trip. How many litres of water is that altogether?
items.e: 4 × 750 = 3,000 mL. 1 L = 1,000 mL, so 3,000 mL = 3 L. (3,000 L forgets to change the unit, and 30 L uses 1 L = 100 mL.)

items.q: Diya is 1.35 m tall. How tall is she in centimetres?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 1.35 × 100 = 135 cm. (13.5 cm multiplies by 10, and 1,350 cm by 1,000.)

items.q: A pumpkin from a farm stand has a mass of 4.25 kg. What is its mass in grams?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so 4.25 × 1,000 = 4,250 g. (425 g multiplies by 100, and 4,025 g reads 0.25 kg as 25 g.)

items.q: Nikhil’s hockey stick is 1.5 m long. His little sister’s stick is 95 cm long. How much longer is Nikhil’s stick, in centimetres?
items.e: 1.5 m = 150 cm. 150 − 95 = 55 cm. (93.5 cm takes 1.5 from 95 without converting, 80 cm uses 1.5 m = 15 cm, and 10 cm uses 1.5 m = 105 cm.)

items.q: Arjun runs 3 laps of a 400 m track. Then he runs 2 km more. How many metres does he run in all?
items.e: 3 × 400 = 1,200 m. 2 km = 2,000 m. 1,200 + 2,000 = 3,200 m. (1,400 m uses 2 km = 200 m, 1,220 m uses 2 km = 20 m, and 1,202 m forgets to convert the 2 km.)
